/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=5120
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  stop)
    init_ws; which="${1:-all}"
    if [ "$which" = all ]; then
      bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; echo \"stopped \$u\"; done" </dev/null
    else
      bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") && echo stopped nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which" </dev/null
    fi ;;

  logs)
    init_ws; which=dev; [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "${1:0:1}" != - ] && { which="$1"; shift; }
    bh_ssh "journalctl --no-pager -o cat -u $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") $(q "${@:--n100}")" ;;

  tunnel)
    rport="${1:?usage: devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]}"; lport="${2:-$rport}"
    say "forwarding primary 127.0.0.1:$lport -> node-2 127.0.0.1:$rport (Ctrl-C to close)"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    exec ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L "127.0.0.1:$lport:127.0.0.1:$rport" "$BUILD_HOST" ;;

  pull)
    init_ws; src="${1:?usage: devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]}"; dst="${2:-.}"
    case "$src" in /*|*..*) die "path must be relative to the workspace" ;; esac
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    rsync -a --compress -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/$src" "$dst" ;;

  db)
    init_ws; ensure_remote
    case "${1:-info}" in
      push)  push_files; deps 0; run_remote 0 900 npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate ;;
      reset) bh_ssh ". /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env; export PGPASSWORD=\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD; dropdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U \$AGENT_PGUSER --if-exists --force $DBNAME && createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U \$AGENT_PGUSER $DBNAME && echo recreated $DBNAME" </dev/null
             say "now: scripts/devhost db push" ;;
      info)  echo "throwaway database $DBNAME on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433 (role nxeon_agent); DATABASE_URL is preset for every devhost command" ;;
      *) die "usage: devhost db push|reset|info" ;;
    esac ;;

  env)
    init_ws; ensure_remote
    case "${1:-list}" in
      list) bh_ssh "sed -E 's/^([A-Z0-9_]*(SECRET|PASSWORD|TOKEN|KEY|URL)[A-Z0-9_]*)=.*/\1=<set>/' $(q "$ENVF")" </dev/null ;;
      set)
        kv="${2:?usage: devhost env set KEY=VALUE}"; k="${kv%%=*}"; v="${kv#*=}"
        case "$k" in ""|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) die "bad key $k" ;; DATABASE_URL) die "DATABASE_URL is fixed to the throwaway DB" ;; esac
        # Refuse anything that is a live production value (compared here, never printed).
        for f in /opt/nxeon/.env /opt/nxeon-staging/.env; do
          [ -r "$f" ] && [ ${#v} -ge 12 ] && cut -d= -f2- "$f" | tr -d '"'"'" | grep -qxF -- "$v" && die "refusing: that value is a live value from $f. devhost never gets production/staging credentials."
        done
        printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" | bh_ssh "f=$(q "$ENVF"); grep -v '^$k=' \"\$f\" > \"\$f.tmp\" || true; cat >> \"\$f.tmp\"; chmod 600 \"\$f.tmp\"; mv \"\$f.tmp\" \"\$f\"" && say "set $k for $NAME" ;;
      unset) k="${2:?key}"; case "$k" in DATABASE_URL|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) die "cannot unset $k";; esac
             bh_ssh "f=$(q "$ENVF"); grep -v '^$k=' \"\$f\" > \"\$f.tmp\" || true; chmod 600 \"\$f.tmp\"; mv \"\$f.tmp\" \"\$f\"" </dev/null && say "unset $k" ;;
      *) die "usage: devhost env list|set KEY=VALUE|unset KEY" ;;
    esac ;;

  rm)
    init_ws
    bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; done
      . /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env; PGPASSWORD=\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD dropdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U \$AGENT_PGUSER --if-exists --force $DBNAME
      rm -rf -- $(q "$WS") $(q "$ENVF") && echo removed $NAME" </dev/null ;;

  ls)
    bh_ssh "shopt -s nullglob; cd $BH_ROOT/wt 2>/dev/null && for d in */; do d=\${d%/}; printf '%-42s %8s  %s\n' \"\$d\" \"\$(du -sh \"\$d\" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)\" \"\$(cat \"\$d/.devhost-owner\" 2>/dev/null)\"; done" </dev/null ;;

  status)
    bh_ssh "bash -s" <<'EOF'
echo "node-2: $(uptime | sed 's/.*load/load/')"
awk '/MemAvailable/{printf "MemAvailable: %d MB\n", $2/1024}' /proc/meminfo
for s in nxeon-build.slice nxeon-build-prod.slice nxeon-build-agents.slice; do
  set -- $(systemctl show -P MemoryCurrent "$s") $(systemctl show -P MemoryPeak "$s") $(systemctl show -P CPUUsageNSec "$s")
  printf '%-26s mem %6s MB (peak %6s MB)  cpu %8s s\n' "$s" $(( ${1:-0} / 1048576 )) $(( ${2:-0} / 1048576 )) $(( ${3:-0} / 1000000000 ))
done
echo "build lock: $(flock -n /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock true && echo free || echo HELD)"
echo "running units:"; systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-*' 'nxeon-release-*' 'nxeon-run-*' | awk '{print "  "$1}'
EOF
    ;;

  *) die "unknown command '$cmd' (scripts/devhost help)" ;;
esac

## Cyrus asset catalog (v2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r14-catalog` (2026-10-10). Code: `lib/cyrus/library/v2/`. Owner report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/M-catalog-v2.md`. **Library code + one migration file (not applied). No route, no UI, no flag, nothing deployed, no paid model call.**

The metadata, tagging and retrieval layer that lets Cyrus (Claude in the build service) pick the right asset for a situation, at near-zero tokens per asset. It sits on top of the existing unified library (`lib/cyrus/library`, R1): the sound taxonomy, texture taxonomy, plan gate and `browseLibrary` are reused, not replaced.

### 1. CatalogEntry v1 (`entry.ts`, JSON Schema `catalog-entry.v1.schema.json`)
- `id` = sha256 of the bytes (also the dedupe key); referenced everywhere else as `cat:<sha256>`.
- `kind` model | texture-set | texture | sprite | hdri | decal | sound | music; `title` (<=80), `shortDescription` (<=140), `tags` (controlled vocabulary, `vocab.json`) + `freeTags` (<=8), `categories {primary, secondary[<=3]}` (`<domain>/<sub>`; `sound/*` = the sound taxonomy ids, `pixel/*` = the texture-library categories), `useFor` (situation ids, e.g. `gunshot-sound`, `scifi-crate-prop`, `ston
- `quality {score 0-100, version cq-1, method, measured share, checks[]}` (`quality.ts`): weighted pass ratio of the MEASURED checks x (0.4 + 0.6 x measured share); a hard fail (corrupt, silent audio, zero triangles) caps at 20. Model: format, triangles (warn > 50k, fail > 300k), size, materials, real-world scale vs the category; PBR: maps, normal convention, resolution, physical size; 2D: dimensi
- `games {game: {fit good|ok|no, reason, notes, transform[]}}` from each game's `AssetProfile` (`fit.ts`). New optional `AssetProfile.catalog` hints (`lib/cyrus/adapters/asset-profile.ts`): accepted kinds (native/convert/none + reasons), style affinity, triangle budgets, texture sizes, audio target. Only Minecraft declares them today: sounds/music `good` (mono Ogg transcode), 16/32/64 px square sp
- `tech` (tris, vertices, meshes, materials, bounds in metres, rigged, animations; width/height, PBR maps, alpha, tileable, physical size; audio duration, rate, channels, bit depth, peak, true peak, LUFS, silence ratio, loopable heuristic, centroid, transient/sustained), `licence {tier cc0|cc-by|proprietary-nxeon|user-contributed, spdx, sourceUrl, attribution, status}`, `provenance`, `legalClass` 

### 2. Enrichment pipeline

While that runs, I'll start sketching the SQLite schema for the posting-based index, defining tables for metadata and entries with fields for id, kind, status, tier, quality, duplicates, and grouping info.

For search efficiency, I'm figuring out how to compute document frequency without heavy caching overhead—likely just an in-process cache cleared on writes rather than maintaining a separate df table, since range scans on 38k postings are fast enough already. For the actual query logic, I'm working through how to group terms, score matches with decay for partial matches, and aggregate results per document in JS after the SQL grouping step.

Now I'm working through the filtering logic: after scoring candidates, I need to apply share and quality filters before computing final scores, which means fetching filter columns for potentially tens of thousands of candidate rids. I'm weighing whether to chunk the IN query or use a temp table joined against the entry table to avoid the overhead of fetching unfiltered columns for every candidate.

Then I need the ranking formula itself — combining game fitness weight (good/ok/no/unknown), quality score, and normalized text score — all computed within one SQL query that also handles group collapsing and ordering, so I can return the final sorted (rid, score, group) results in a single pass.

Still writing scoring query...

Still mapping the games fit lookup via JSON extraction, and I need to replicate the empty-tiers-means-nothing-passes logic in SQL. For the no-text query case, I'm weighing whether fetching ~58k rows from node:sqlite is fast enough versus pushing more of the ranking/ordering work into the SQL query itself.

For group collapsing, I can use window functions: a ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by group (or row id if ungrouped) ordered by rank/quality/id picks the representative, while a COUNT(*) over the same partition gives the group size, and the overall total still needs to match the pre-collapse hit count from the filtered set before grouping.

For text queries, normalizing rank requires dividing by the max text score across all results, which I can get via a MAX() window function over the whole result set. SQLite supports window functions and node:sqlite bundles a recent enough version, so I think the entire ranking, collapsing, and pagination pipeline can live in SQL, only pulling JSON for the final page of row ids -- though I'm wary that computing rank in SQL versus JS could hit floating-point ordering differences that break tie-break parity with the existing sort by rank, quality, then id.

For idf and df, I need to make sure the SQLite computation using doc counts and posting table counts matches the in-memory version exactly, including treating all entries (not just published) as part of N. For upserts, I'm planning to delete and reinsert postings per rid, but with ~61k entries and ~30 terms each that's roughly 2M posting rows, so I want to check the insert time and resulting DB size stay reasonable compared to the current FTS build time.

Now I'm writing sqlite-index.ts v2, keeping the same export name and signature but bumping the schema version. If an older schema (with entry_fts) is detected, I'll just drop those tables entirely and let the caller treat it as needing a rebuild, rather than trying to migrate.

content.thinking:
I'm checking that the idf binding as a parameter value keeps the SQL shape consistent for prepared statement reuse, and verifying the memory index's finish() sort order and text normalization match the SQL logic, including how textScore handles zero terms versus low share cases.

Confirming that filters, status defaults, tier checks, tag matching, and category prefix/exact logic all align between the in-memory implementation and the SQL equivalent. With that verified, I'm moving on to writing the backend modules, starting with a flags module that defines library configuration flags and a function to derive them from environment variables like enabling the backend, contribution mode, storage type, and URL secrets.

Now I'm defining the object store module, including a local implementation that validates sha256-based keys and organizes files into subdirectories by hash prefix, plus the environment variables needed for S3 and local storage configuration.

Still writing S3ObjectStore methods...

For StagingSource, I'm designing a read-only accessor that resolves entry paths safely inside the root (guarding against traversal or symlink escapes via realpath checks), confirms file existence, and verifies content by comparing sha256 hashes against the entry id when reading.

Now I'm sketching the recipe system in derive.ts — defining recipe IDs and a shared Recipe type covering input kinds, formats, output mime/size limits, and the tool used (JS, ffmpeg, PIL, or gltf-transform), each with a run function that transforms input bytes into output bytes. I'm starting with the thumb-png@1 recipe, decoding PNGs up to a max resolution in pure JS.

Still writing recipe logic...

I'm pinning the gltf-transform optimize command with meshopt compression, noting the tool must be pre-installed since missing tools surface as `tool_missing` errors rather than failing silently. I'm also sketching the ToolRunner interface for spawning binaries safely and beginning the LibraryStore class definition.

Within LibraryStore, I'm fleshing out methods: `original()` tries the object store first, falls back to staging with verification and optional persistence; `derivative()` lazily checks the derivative index, regenerates via recipe if missing while enforcing capability checks before caching; `recipesFor()` maps entries to applicable recipes; and I'm starting on a `sweep()` method for cleanup logic.

Now I'm defining retention rules—derivatives unused past a TTL get deleted along with orphaned objects, and removed-entry originals are purged after a grace period, but only from the object store, never staging. I'm also setting per-kind size caps for originals and derivatives (like 64MB for models, 512KB for thumbnails) that trigger a `too_large` refusal, sketching the DerivativeIndex interface with memory and Postgres implementations, and moving into planning serve.ts for signed URLs and access decisions.

Removed entries should return 410 rather than 404, and raw audio originals must never be served at all—only the preview-ogg variant is allowed, and only when the tier isn't proprietary-nxeon or the sound has been cleared. For proprietary-nxeon tier specifically, every variant is refused unless explicitly cleared, with originals permanently blocked. Browsing itself needs a plan gate too, checking signed-in status and plan against the library kind, with sound requiring Saka+ and visuals open to all models.

Thumbnails follow the same browse gate as the main content. For non-audio assets, serving the original is fine since it's either CC0 or user-contributed, so redistribution isn't a concern—this supports the "use in project" download flow. Tokens should have a max TTL of 900 seconds (default 300), and at request time the route needs to verify the signed claims subject matches the current viewer's session before serving the file, returning 403 otherwise.

I'm leaning toward hashing the user id into an opaque sub (HMAC-based) so raw user ids never leak into token URLs. Since tokens are short-lived, I can trust the plan/tier decision captured at sign-time rather than re-querying it on fetch, but I still want to re-verify entry status and variant rules (like refusing raw audio) before streaming bytes with appropriate cache headers and content-type from the recipe.

I need to figure out where the route pulls the library and catalog stores from — likely a backend factory that builds from env and the host db, kept server-only. I also need to wire up a sign endpoint so the library browser can request URLs, which means checking what API routes already exist for library browsing to see how they handle viewer plan lookups.

Now I'm working out how Prisma's raw query interface handles parameterized placeholders for pg, including JSONB casting and array parameters.

For bulk upserts, I realize using `jsonb_to_recordset` with a single JSON parameter lets me insert or update thousands of rows at once without hitting parameter limits, which I'll apply to both catalog entries and terms. Then I'm building the Postgres-backed store implementing the catalog interfaces, and sketching the full-text search SQL using CTEs that score term matches, aggregate weighted sums, filter by coverage threshold, and join against the entries table to compute final ranking.

For IDF calculation I need the document count N and per-term document frequency df -- df I'll fetch in one batched query grouping term counts, while N can be cached briefly with a short TTL and invalidated on writes to keep it accurate without re-counting every query.

For filters, I'm handling duplicateOf, status, kind, tier, and quality as straightforward WHERE clauses, but for tag matching I'll use `jsonb_exists` instead of the `?` operator to avoid any ambiguity with Prisma's parameter placeholders.

For useFor, categories, and other array-based fields, I'm using `jsonb_exists_any` and checking both primary and secondary category fields, with prefix matching via `starts_with` to safely handle category paths without LIKE wildcard conflicts.

I'm also planning a fuzzy-match fallback using pg_trgm's similarity function when exact searches return nothing, gracefully skipping it if the extension isn't installed, and setting up an admin-only full-text search using tsvector/websearch_to_tsquery over the searchable text.

The searchText field itself should be a lowercase concatenation of title, description, tags, categories, and other fields, giving the PG implementation a straightforward target column. I'm also sketching a generic Sql interface with query/exec methods, plus a Prisma-backed implementation wrapping raw query execution.

I need to handle type conversions carefully: bigint counts from COUNT(*) need converting to Number, floats need explicit casts, and timestamps are trickiest since Prisma's Date serialization doesn't cleanly match raw SQL timestamp columns — passing ISO strings with explicit `::timestamp` casts is the safer approach.

Now I'm working out the vocab.json merge strategy for categories, tags, synonyms, and useFor across proposals, deciding whether to keep or replace my earlier motion category additions in favor of the proposal's naming, then turning to quality checks per motion kind (flipbook frame/grid/fps validation, particle-texture image checks, animation-clip duration and keyframe checks, animated-model clip counts) and thinking through whether Minecraft's lowering path can actually support flipbook-style animated textures via resource pack mechanics.

I should be careful with kind words since matching "particle" could also hit effect-related tags, causing confusion—better to stick to safer terms like "flipbook", "spritesheet", "animation" mapped to animation-clip/animated-model, and "preset" mapped to motion-preset/effect-preset, skipping ambiguous ones like "clip" and "effect". ## Cyrus asset library backend

Branch `feature/cyrus-r26-library` (2026-10-10). Code: `lib/cyrus/library/backend/` + the SQLite index v2 (`lib/cyrus/library/v2/sqlite-index.ts`) + motion/effect kinds in catalog v2. Owner report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/W-library-backend.md`. **Everything is behind OFF switches. Migration file not applied. Nothing deployed, no flag flipped, no paid model call.** Owner rules applied: CC0-only library (CC-BY rows are not imported), no creator credit shown, contribution of assets made in Cyrus is automatic after the content filters, never game-derived / third-party / imported / uploaded / template / derived content.

### Switches (env, all off)
`CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND=1` (master: the `/api/cyrus/library/v2/*` routes answer, otherwise 404), `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE=1` (automatic contribution writes; needs the master switch), `CYRUS_LIBRARY_STORE=off|local|s3` (+ `CYRUS_LIBRARY_LOCAL_DIR`, or `CYRUS_LIBRARY_S3_ENDPOINT/_BUCKET/_REGION/_ACCESS_KEY_ID/_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/_PREFIX`), `CYRUS_LIBRARY_STAGING_DIR` (read-only source of staged originals), `CYRUS_LIBRARY_URL_SECRET` (>= 32 chars, signs file URLs), tool paths `CYRUS_LIBRARY_FFMPEG`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_PYTHON` (Pillow), `CYRUS_LIBRARY_GLTF_TRANSFORM`. The existing `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` still gates the owner's proprietary SFX library.

input.content:
# W: Cyrus asset library backend (r26, 2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r26-library` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r26`, latest `feature/cyrus-r2` merged). Code `lib/cyrus/library/backend/`, SQLite index v2, motion kinds in catalog v2. Docs "Cyrus asset library backend". **Nothing deployed, no migration run, no flag flipped, no paid model call.** Switches: `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_STORE`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_URL_SECRET` (all off).

## What was built
1. **Storage**: content-addressed object store (local disk, S3 with the pack host's SigV4, private), read-only staging source (path-confined, hash-checked), per-kind caps, 30-day retention sweep. Derivatives generated lazily by deterministic recipes: `thumb@1` (pure-JS PNG / pinned Pillow for JPEG), `preview-ogg@1` (fixed ffmpeg argv), `glb-opt@1`, `bundle@1` (folder sets). Signed, 5-minute, viewer-scoped URLs re-checked at fetch; raw audio never served; the proprietary SFX library never as originals and only when cleared.
2. **Index**: Postgres tables (migration file, not applied), posting index with the same ranking as the memory index, pg_trgm typo fallback, full-text admin find, idempotent importer. **SQLite index rewritten** (posting lists, one SQL statement).
3. **Contribution**: automatic, after `libraryEligible` and strict filters; status published / held / removed; hold queue (real-weapon, trademark, extremist, drugs, mature violence); exact + near dedupe (image dhash, audio envelope, glb facts, motion JSON); a removed hash cannot be re-contributed; provenance and legal class kept.
4. **Reports / takedown**: legal report or 3 reporters hold; takedown removes now, purges derivatives, marks dependents; **dependent mods keep building from their own copy, not plan-gated** (tested in memory and on Postgres).
5. **Use in project**: `cat:<sha256>` slot + project copy + dependents record; sounds Saka+, visuals All models; keeping never gated.
6. **Admin**: read model (counts by kind/tier/status, hold queue, takedown log) inside `/api/admin/cyrus/ops` when the switch is on. No page.
7. **Motion kinds** (coordinator request): flipbook, particle-texture, animation-clip, animated-model, motion-preset, effect-preset; vocabulary proposal merged; `provenance.via` max 400.

## Ran (node-2 unless noted)
| What | Result |
|---|---|
| Old FTS5 index, 60,970 entries | worst 142 ms (17 s **not reproduced**), top-8 equal to memory 2/28 |
| SQLite v2 | worst 92 ms (memory DB) / 143 ms (file), **28/28** identical to memory, exact totals |
| Memory index | 23-376 ms |
| Import dry run | 60,970 valid, 0 invalid, 3.0 s |
| Import real (Postgres + SQLite file) | 469 s, 1,100,093 postings; re-run 4.7 s, 0 written |
| Postgres catalog_search | medians 9-160 ms, worst 323 ms; "wodden dor" finds "Door wooden" |
| Prisma check | `db push` drops a hand-written GIN index on a plain column; shipped indexes are expression indexes, diff empty |
| Derivatives, 134 staged CC0 assets | thumbs 110/123, bundles 11/11, all cache hits on pass 2; previews/glb-opt: tools missing |
| ffmpeg preview argv, 3 CC0 sounds (primary, tiny) | byte-identical twice |
| Stage A motion pass 2 (1,807) | 98.4 % full, 4 zero-length clips held |
| Stage A motion pass 1 (1,951 CC0, 21 CC-BY out) | 31.1 % full, 68.0 % partial, 0.9 % none |
| Tests | new unit + golden + throwaway-DB suites pass; full Cyrus + builder suite and tsc: see final commit |

## Not run / not built

# W: Cyrus asset library backend (r26, 2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r26-library` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r26`, latest `feature/cyrus-r2` merged). Code `lib/cyrus/library/backend/`, SQLite index v2, motion kinds in catalog v2. Docs "Cyrus asset library backend". **Nothing deployed, no migration run, no flag flipped, no paid model call.** Switches: `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_STORE`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_URL_SECRET` (all off).

## What was built
1. **Storage**: content-addressed object store (local disk, S3 with the pack host's SigV4, private), read-only staging source (path-confined, hash-checked), per-kind caps, 30-day retention sweep. Derivatives generated lazily by deterministic recipes: `thumb@1` (pure-JS PNG / pinned Pillow for JPEG), `preview-ogg@1` (fixed ffmpeg argv), `glb-opt@1`, `bundle@1` (folder sets). Signed, 5-minute, viewer-scoped URLs re-checked at fetch; raw audio never served; the proprietary SFX library never as originals and only when cleared.
2. **Index**: Postgres tables (migration file, not applied), posting index with the same ranking as the memory index, pg_trgm typo fallback, full-text admin find, idempotent importer. **SQLite index rewritten** (posting lists, one SQL statement).
3. **Contribution**: automatic, after `libraryEligible` and strict filters; status published / held / removed; hold queue (real-weapon, trademark, extremist, drugs, mature violence); exact + near dedupe (image dhash, audio envelope, glb facts, motion JSON); a removed hash cannot be re-contributed; provenance and legal class kept.
4. **Reports / takedown**: legal report or 3 reporters hold; takedown removes now, purges derivatives, marks dependents; **dependent mods keep building from their own copy, not plan-gated** (tested in memory and on Postgres).
5. **Use in project**: `cat:<sha256>` slot + project copy + dependents record; sounds Saka+, visuals All models; keeping never gated.
6. **Admin**: read model (counts by kind/tier/status, hold queue, takedown log) inside `/api/admin/cyrus/ops` when the switch is on. No page.
7. **Motion kinds** (coordinator request): flipbook, particle-texture, animation-clip, animated-model, motion-preset, effect-preset; vocabulary proposal merged; `provenance.via` max 400.
